verses.text: One day, as Jesus was teaching the people in the temple and preaching the good news, the chief priests and the teachers of the law came up with the elders.
They said, "Tell us, by what authority are you doing these things? Who gave you this authority?"
He answered, "I will also ask you one question. Tell me:
John's baptism, was it from heaven, or from people?"
They talked it over among themselves. "If we say, 'From heaven,' he will ask, 'Then why did you not believe him?'
But if we say, 'From people,' all the people will stone us, because they are convinced that John was a prophet."
So they answered that they did not know where it was from.
Jesus said, "Then I will not tell you by what authority I do these things."
Then he told the people this story. "A man planted a vineyard, rented it to some farmers, and went away to another country for a long time.
At harvest time he sent a servant to the farmers to collect his share of the fruit. But the farmers beat him and sent him away with nothing.
He sent another servant, and they beat him too, treated him shamefully, and sent him away with nothing.
He sent a third, and they wounded him and threw him out.
Then the owner of the vineyard said, 'What shall I do? I will send my son, whom I love. Maybe they will respect him.'
But when the farmers saw him, they talked it over. 'This is the heir,' they said. 'Let us kill him, so that the inheritance will be ours.'
So they threw him out of the vineyard and killed him. What then will the owner of the vineyard do to them?
He will come and kill those farmers and give the vineyard to others." When the people heard this, they said, "May that never happen!"
Jesus looked straight at them and said, "Then what does this writing mean: 'The stone the builders rejected has become the chief cornerstone'?
Everyone who falls on that stone will be broken to pieces, and anyone it falls on will be crushed."
The chief priests and the teachers of the law wanted to arrest him right then, but they were afraid of the people. They knew he had told this story against them.
So they watched him and sent spies who pretended to be honest. They hoped to catch Jesus in something he said, so they could hand him over to the power and authority of the governor.
The spies asked him, "Teacher, we know that you speak and teach what is right. You do not favour anyone, but teach the way of God truly.
Is it right for us to pay taxes to Caesar, or not?"
He saw through their trick and said, "Why are you testing me?
Show me a denarius. Whose image and name are on it?" "Caesar's," they replied.
He said, "Then give to Caesar what belongs to Caesar, and give to God what belongs to God."
They could not trap him in what he said in front of the people. Amazed at his answer, they became silent.
Some of the Sadducees, who say there is no resurrection, came to him with a question.
"Teacher," they said, "Moses wrote for us that if a man's brother dies and leaves a wife but no child, the man must marry the widow and raise up children for his brother.
Now there were seven brothers. The first married a woman and died childless.
The second married her, and he also died childless.
Then the third married her, and in the same way all seven died, leaving no children.
Finally the woman also died.
So in the resurrection, whose wife will she be? All seven were married to her."
Jesus replied, "The people of this age marry and are given in marriage.
But those who are counted worthy to share in the age to come, and in the resurrection from the dead, will neither marry nor be given in marriage.
They cannot die any more, because they are like the angels. They are God's children, because they are children of the resurrection.
But that the dead are raised, even Moses showed at the bush, when he calls the Lord 'the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.'
He is not the God of the dead, but of the living, because all are alive to him."
Some of the teachers of the law said, "Teacher, you have spoken well."
And they did not dare to ask him any more questions.
Then Jesus said to them, "Why do people say that the Christ is David's son?
David himself says in the book of Psalms, 'The Lord said to my Lord, "Sit at my right hand
until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet."'
David calls him Lord. So how can he be his son?"
While all the people were listening, Jesus said to his followers,

"Watch out for the teachers of the law. They like to walk around in long robes, and they love to be greeted in the market places, and to have the best seats in the synagogues and the places of honour at feasts.
They take over widows' houses, and for a pretence they make long prayers. These men will be punished most severely."
